items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: getting people like Clark Terry and Bob to go up there and bring his charts and to work with them

ctx.x: You said it pretty well. You really did. I think sometimes academics may be threatened by people who have made their living playing the music instead of just teaching about it. That that may be a threat to them. But there are some inroads being made in that.

I’d like to think so. And there are certainly teachers, I mean there’s one particular teacher at the University of New Hampshire who is very encouraging and is always getting people like Clark Terry and Bob to go up there and bring his charts and to work with them. And I think that this is one thing that you can do. You can certainly set aside some time. And I think another problem that is part of our society, Monk, is that students are being called upon to give far too many hours for other extracurricular…
And they could be a great audience too.
